newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen down in near term.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen down in near term.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded after a four-session fall but analysts said that even though growth was possible on Thursday the market was soon likely to continue the mild downward correction begun late last month.

Analysts said the slightly stronger buying after price fixing meant the market could extend gains for a session or two but that the continued outperformance by speculative small-cap stocks and continuous trade dips augured falls.
"With (most active) Elektrim and Bank Slaski falling the situation doesn't look too good," said Sebastian Buczek of ING BSK Asset Management.
Elektrim and Bank Slaski fell 3.2 percent and 0.9 percent respectively at the regular session.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 17,539.9 points and turnover rose 10.6 percent to 190.6 zlotys on all three markets.
Analysts said the main market, which reached a 35-month high on February 18 at 18,339.4 points, could fall as low as 16,000 points before rebounding.
"The market needs to be cheaper to have a platform for a more significant rebound," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Analysts said top gainer Espebepe surged 9.1 percent as the stock continued to vacillate before the ailing firm's creditors meet on March 14 to discuss a possible debt restructuring deal.
They said ComputerLand jumped 6.7 percent after Tuesday's news it would market and sell Siemens Nixdorf goods.
NFI units were flat at the regular session at 163 zlotys and fell 0.3 percent to 161 zlotys in 33.7- million-zloty continuous trade where most stocks fell in a 6.9-million-zloty turnover.
